article.headline: Duolingo Climbs 2% As CEO Says ChatGPT Won't Replace The App
article.deck: Duolingo closed past the 167.48 buy point of a 10-week cup, inside a buy range that runs to 175.85.
body: Duolingo rose 3.44, or 2.1%, to 168.75 on Monday and closed past the 167.48 buy point of a 10-week cup, the one breakout among the day's stories. The cup ran 25.2% deep, from a Sept. 3 rim to a Nov. 3 low of 125.12. The close sits 0.8% above the buy point, and the buy range runs to 175.85. Volume was 2,208,353 shares, 1.77x the 50-day average. The stock moved up on a day the Nasdaq fell 2.5%. After hours it traded at 168.29, down 0.3%.

The cup sits inside a far bigger correction: Duolingo remains well below its Aug. 8, 2025 peak of 415.76, and it hit 87.89 on Apr. 9. It is 20.9% under its 52-week high of 213.37. The stock closed 15.2% above its 50-day line at 146.45 and 0.99 ATRs from the 21-day line at 151.93, so the move is not stretched. RS rank is 92 of 99 on the desk's list, though the RS line is still 25.6% below its high. The stock is down 3.8% this year and 9.5% over 12 months.

The quarters are mixed. September-quarter EPS was 0.54, down 90.9% from a year earlier, on revenue of $309.0 million, up 13.7%. EPS has slipped in each quarter shown, from 0.90 to 0.89, 0.66 and 0.54, while revenue climbed from $282.9 million to $309.0 million. The forward P/E is 21.6 on a market cap of about $8.0 billion.

Duolingo's CEO told Yahoo Finance that ChatGPT and live translation won't replace the app. A Simply Wall St. headline said the stock faces a valuation test following class action lawsuits and AI concerns.
A close back under 167.48 would make this a stalled breakout.
article.watch: Whether Duolingo holds 167.48 while it trades under the 175.85 top of the buy range.

article.headline: Fastenal Holds Near 52-Week High While The Market Sells Off
article.deck: Fastenal is 3.9% past the 53.02 buy point of a 12-week flat base, near the 55.67 top of its buy range.
body: Fastenal slipped 0.08, or 0.1%, to 55.11 on Monday while the S&P 500 fell 1.9%. The stock broke out Nov. 4 from a 12-week flat base 10.6% deep, clearing a 53.02 buy point in a session that traded 1.48x its 50-day average volume. The close sits 3.9% above the buy point, inside a buy range that tops out at 55.67. Monday's volume was 8,261,750 shares, 1.1x the 50-day average. After hours the stock traded at 55.33, up 0.4%.

Eight sessions after the breakout, Fastenal is 2.1% below its 52-week high of 56.27. It closed 7.3% above the 50-day line at 51.38 and 1.13 ATRs above the 21-day line at 53.35, an intact trend and not a stretched one. The RS line hit a new high, and the stock carries an RS rank of 81 of 99 on the desk's list. It is up 37.3% this year and 35.2% over 12 months.

September-quarter EPS rose 20.7% to 0.35 on revenue of $2.46 billion, up 15.5%. EPS rose in each quarter shown, from 0.26 to 0.30, 0.33 and 0.35, and revenue from $2.03 billion to $2.46 billion. The next report is due Jan. 19. The market values the company at $63.2 billion, 38.9 times forward earnings.

Zacks noted the stock is up 10.3% since its last earnings report, and 24/7 Wall St. wrote that the shares are up 35% in 2026. Investor's Business Daily reported that Grainger surged on its best revenue growth in five years on Nov. 4, the day Fastenal broke out.
A close above 55.67 would put the stock past the buy range; a close under 53.02 would undo the breakout.

article.headline: Chime Joins S&P MidCap 400 And Climbs Toward Its 52-Week High
article.deck: Chime is 3.8% below the 35.65 buy point of a 10-week cup, buy range to 37.43, and already trades 10% above its 31.17 handle high, the early entry.
body: Chime Financial runs a consumer bank on a phone. It offers checking accounts and debit cards, fee-free mobile banking under Chime Plus, short-term cash products such as SpotMe, MyPay and Instant Loans, and credit-building cards with FICO score tracking, sold mainly to U.S. consumers.

The growth is in the top line. September-quarter revenue reached $718.0 million, up 32.1% from a year earlier, and revenue has risen in each of the four quarters shown: $596.4 million, $647.4 million, $669.8 million and $718.0 million. Earnings have turned positive. The company lost 12 cents a share in the December 2025 quarter, then earned 13 cents, 7 cents and 11 cents.
The market pays $13.16 billion for the company, 30.1 times trailing earnings and 21.3 times forward earnings.

The stock rose 0.74, or 2.2%, to 34.29 on Monday as the Nasdaq fell 2.5%. Volume was 15,960,188 shares, 2.88x the 50-day average. Chime is 3.5% below its 52-week high of 35.55 and is working on the right side of a 10-week cup 27.1% deep, with a low of 25.92 on Sept. 28. The buy point is 35.65, ten cents over that high and 3.8% above the close, and the buy range runs to 37.43. The stock already cleared a handle high of 31.17 from Oct. 20, the early entry, and now trades 10% above it.

The RS line hit a new high Monday, ahead of the price, and the stock ranks 98 of 99 on the desk's list. It closed 14.5% above its 50-day line at 29.94 and 2.18 ATRs above the 21-day line at 31.07, toward the stretched end but under 3. Chime is up 36.2% this year and 78.7% over 12 months, and it leads the desk's recent-IPO group.

The news ran Chime's way last week. Investing.com reported the stock rose after the announcement that it will join the S&P MidCap 400. Simply Wall St. ran headlines on the company's raised 2026 outlook, one saying the stock looks rich after it and another saying it could be 22% undervalued as guidance and results reset the debate.
All of it comes in a market the desk labels in correction, with the Nasdaq 6.8% below its 50-day line and 6.5 weighted distribution days on the count.
article.watch: A close above 35.65, ten cents over the 35.55 52-week high.

chief.verdict: The tape is in correction and the leaders say so: the Nasdaq sits 6.8% under its 50-day and 11.6% off its high, ai chips have only 12% of names above the 50-day, and the groups holding up are healthcare and megacap. The setups worth owning are slow, defensive bases with a rising RS line, not the growth breakouts, and today's lone fresh breakout (DUOL) came from a lagging RS line and a -90.9% earnings quarter. Risk leans down; anything bought here has to prove itself fast.
chief.market: With the S&P 500 at 6 distribution days (weighted 6.0) and the Nasdaq at 5 (weighted 6.5) and the market in correction, keep exposure light, take only the cleanest pivots in small size, and stay mostly in cash until the indexes reclaim their 50-day lines.

picks.why: The cleanest chart on the desk: a 12-week flat base only 10.6% deep, a breakout on 1.48 times volume, and an RS line at a new high while the S&P 500 fell 1.9% and FAST gave up just 0.1%. Earnings are up 20.7% and sales 15.5%, and the next report is not until 2027-01-19. The risk is price: at 55.11 it is 3.9% past the buy point and near the 55.67 top of the range.
picks.entry: Don't chase near 55.67; buy a pullback toward the 53.02 buy point and the 21-day line at 53.35 that holds on quiet volume, and cut it on a close back under 53.02.

picks.why: The 30-week cup broke out on 2.47 times volume, and today's 1.1% dip came on 0.65 times volume, which is how a pullback in a healthy breakout should look. RS rank is 91 and energy is one of the few groups with leaders, though the RS line is still 11.7% off its high and the base is 25.7% deep.
picks.entry: Buyable at 305.2 and up to 316.04, best as close to the 300.99 buy point as you can get; a close under the 21-day line at 296.88 says the breakout failed.

picks.why: Leadership is real: RS rank 98, the RS line at a new high, and a 2.2% gain on 2.88 times volume on a day the Nasdaq fell 2.5%. But the 31.17 handle-high early entry is already 10.0% behind the price, so the aggressive buy is gone, and the stock is 14.5% above its 50-day and 2.18 ATRs over its 21-day after the S&P MidCap 400 news pop. The cup is 27.1% deep, so expect volatility.
picks.entry: Wait for the 35.65 buy point on heavy volume, buy up to 37.43 at most, and pass if it can't clear 35.55, the 52-week high, while the market stays in correction.

avoid.why: A breakout 0.8% past 167.48 that is already 15.2% above its 50-day, from a 25.2% deep cup, with the RS line 25.6% off its high, the stock 20.9% under its 52-week high and the last quarter's earnings down 90.9%. That is a rebound in a broken stock, not a leader.

It broke out 23 sessions ago on 0.82 times volume and is still only 0.8% over the 154.26 buy point; it fell 1.8% today and traded at 153.26 after hours, back under the pivot. The breakout has stalled.
It sits 1.0% under the 119.88 buy point with earnings due 2026-11-17, one session away, so buying the pivot now is a coin flip on the report, not a chart trade.

chief.watch: NVDA reports on 2026-11-17 while it trades 26.8% under its 50-day; if the Nasdaq takes a bad reaction as another heavy down day, that makes six distribution days and the case for staying in cash.
